Kento Alpha 0.9.4, build 2224

Kento's own render engine

  • Renders and the Viewer now go through Kento's own render engine, which works out a whole frame at once and runs the comp's separate branches side by side. It's on by default: Settings > Render > Render engine, both rows tagged Recommended.
  • The picture is the same as before, to the last bit. Only the time changes.
  • Heavy comps render much faster: across the show's 33 heavier Writes, about two and a half times as fast. A 274-node show comp renders its frames a shade faster than Nuke.
  • In the Viewer, an edit is shown again in a quarter of a second or less, even on big comps, because the engine keeps what it worked out and redoes only what changed. Zoomed in, it works out only the part on screen.
  • Every node renders through the engine, the deep nodes, the denoiser, Text2, Matte Refine and the stereo nodes included. Rendering several Writes of one comp reuses what the first already worked out.
  • DeepWrite writes its deep files through the engine too, and the Viewer shows deep pictures and each view of a stereo comp through it.
  • EXR, TIFF, PNG, DPX, JPEG and Targa files go through the engine, with the delivery presets' display transforms baked in the same way, and so do a QuickTime's frames.
  • A few things still go the previous way, automatically and with the same picture: a Write (rather than a DeepWrite) of a deep picture, a file other than EXR with channels besides red, green, blue and alpha, and a comp in proxy; and a downscaled Viewer.
  • Each Render engine row explains in plain words what it does, with a tag: Recommended, or Diagnostic for the experiment to leave off. Turn either row off to go back to the previous way.

Comparing in the Viewer

  • The wipe's handles show only with the pointer near its center, fading in and out; the line stays, dimmed until the pointer comes near.
  • Hold Shift while turning the wipe to step by 45 degrees.
  • The wipe's mix square works: drag it to mix A into B on the B side.
  • The pointer no longer vanishes over the compare control or the other on-screen controls, and the move pointers look as they do in other apps (no more four-way star).

Picking colors

  • Click a color row's swatch to open the picker. The color wheel button is gone, so a row with the eyedropper keeps a longer slider.
  • The red, green, blue and alpha toggles sit side by side as framed buttons: a filled square when on, an outline when off.
  • The same across the panels: Settings' swatches open the picker, and a backdrop's last swatch shows a color wheel until a color of its own is chosen.
  • On the Mac the picker is the system's color window, whose eyedropper picks from anywhere on the screen, not just Kento's windows.

The Node Graph

  • Wires stay put: a wire moves only when one of its own nodes moves, not while the Viewer renders or thumbnails arrive. A big comp's graph sits quiet while it works.
  • Transform's node menu is in groups, as Filter's is: Position and size, Lens (with every lens model), Warp, Tracking, and Crop and bounding box.

Fixed and changed

  • A heavy comp whose gizmo turns its picture before a run of blurs no longer shows black in the Viewer for minutes.
  • Comps with DasGrain render and match Nuke: random() in expressions, and Premult and Unpremult with an alpha outside 0 to 1.
  • Merge2's mix and Sharpen read past an input's edge as Nuke does.
  • DeepCrop on a flat picture no longer crashes.
  • With two Viewers open, Roto's Layers panel follows its own node's selection.

Kento Alpha 0.9.3, build 2076

Selecting points in the Viewer

  • Drag a box from empty ground to select points in every tool that has them: CornerPin, Crop, Transform, Radial, Rectangle, Ramp, Text, Tracker, Roto, RotoPaint, GridWarp, SplineWarp, Perspective and a Card's lattice in the 3D view. Shift-drag adds to the selection.
  • Shift-click adds a point or takes it out; a drag on one selected point moves them all, as one undo. Cmd+A selects every point, Esc lets go, and Option with the arrow keys nudges the selection a pixel (Shift, ten).
  • The point a click would take lights up under the pointer, with the move cursor.
  • A GridWarp box can start anywhere in the Viewer, and the warp now reaches past the edge of the image.
  • The Projection's drawn plane: Shift-click or Shift-drag a box round its corners to move several at once, or drag inside the plane to slide it.

Picking colors

  • Every color row of a node with a picture coming in (a Grade, a ColorCorrect and the rest) has an eyedropper beside the color wheel: click the Viewer for a pixel, or drag a box for its average.
  • A box picked over a whole plate is near instant (it took several seconds).
  • The eyedropper and the pick-whip have new icons that look like what they are.

The Viewer

  • Depth, motion vectors, normals, position and uv passes show readably as soon as they're chosen from the layer menu, with no node needed.
  • Switched to an image of another size, the Viewer shows that image's format; its on-screen controls work on any format.
  • The number keys over the Viewer switch its inputs; I and O set the in and out points.
  • Closing a floating Viewer's window puts the view back in the Viewer panel.
  • The wipe, ruler guides and rulers can be dragged with any tool open; an armed eyedropper takes the next click.

The Node Graph and keys

  • W puts a Write in the stream, as the other node keys do, and every node key makes its node as Tab does, with its starting values.
  • Shift-click on a selected node takes it out of the selection. An undo just after a snapped drag puts the nodes back.
  • Import Nuke Script selects and frames what came in.
  • Lists pick as lists do: Shift-click picks a range and Cmd-click adds or takes out one, in Roto's Layers, the Tracker's table, Tracks over time and Perspective's lines. Layers also takes Up, Down and Cmd+A.
  • Cmd+, opens Settings.
  • The frame step keys stop at the ends of the range.

Number fields

  • A drag scrubs by the digit under the pointer, keeping the digits after it; Up and Down step the digit after the cursor.
  • Esc while typing puts the value back.

Perspective and Lens

  • Both open on a start card for a first-time user, with the next step named and the expert sections closed.
  • Perspective lists the current set's lines, one a row: select, change direction, leave one out of the solve or delete it.
  • Lens: grid shoots of several frames solved together, dot and line charts beside the checkerboard, an anamorphic lens from lines in the plate, and a learned first guess (downloaded the first time it's asked for).

Fixed and changed

  • Use for the comp on a Read sets the comp's format to the plate's size; Project settings opens from the Node Graph; Custom size in the format menus.
  • Every menu item works from the menu: Viewer > Rulers, the overlays, Proxy, Downscale and Snap to grid did nothing there.
  • The Curve Editor frames its keys clear of the ruler, and a drag on a key moves the key.
  • The Dope Sheet takes Cmd+A and Esc; file lists find a file as you type its name.
  • Looks follow the comp's color configuration.
  • Gizmos that add their own layers (L_ChannelSolo) render.
  • Switching workspaces no longer leaves errors behind.
  • The Node tab's bookmark is the star on the node, read from and written to .nk files.

Kento Alpha 0.9.2, build 1987

New: Perspective

  • A new Perspective node (Transform menu). Draw lines along a plate's edges, each on its axis, and it works out the vanishing points, the horizon and the camera: focal length with its plus-or-minus, tilt, roll and field of view, live as you draw. Lines slide onto the plate's edge when you let go (Shift leaves them where drawn).
  • Find lines finds the plate's straight edges on the frame; click one to add it on the axis it agrees with.
  • Line sets: lock a set to keep its lines over the plate as a reference for a lineup. Locked sets show in every Viewer showing the plate or anything below it.
  • Match to another plate compares two plates' cameras in words and makes the CornerPin2D or Transform that lines one up with the other. Make Camera makes a camera linked to the solve.
  • Measure: set one known height and the panel shows the camera's height; each Measure line reads the height of what it spans.
  • Drag a vanishing point to swing its lines; a hand-drawn horizon moves, turns and levels, and can keep the ground's vanishing points on it. With one axis and the horizon, type the focal length.

New: Lens

  • A new Lens node (Transform menu): takes a lens's distortion out of a plate or puts it back, as the picture, an STMap or both. The distortion is a curve to drag, with sliders beside it, and the row says barrel or pincushion.
  • Work it out from a lens grid, from lines drawn on the plate, or from the shot's camera tracks; the Report shows each corner's leftover error, the straightened lines, or the camera solve's stages.
  • The lens card names the lens the plate was most likely shot on, from its metadata (movies' too), the film back worked out from the plate's size and file name, and the show's lens library. Use this lens hands it to a CameraTracker, each value Fixed or Refine.
  • Write STMaps and Save to the lens library; the Viewer shows the grid as the lens bends it, the box, and the lens center to drag.
  • LensDistortion2 renders every model on its preset menu as scripts set them, and Detect and Solve work it out from a checkerboard. Its STMap output now covers the whole frame.
  • The two lens-model nodes from matchmove scripts, Classic LD and Radial Standard degree 4, now render instead of being left out.
  • A CameraTracker set to Unknown Lens works the lens out with the camera, and with an anamorphic lens its two asymmetric values too.

Faster

  • PixelKernel on the processor is now compiled the first time it renders: the painterly kernel went from 48 seconds an HD frame to under one. On a Mac without the command-line developer tools, Kento offers to install them.
  • Merge works its operations a tile at a time, faster with the same picture.

Fixed and changed

  • FillMat renders: it fills the chosen channels with its color, the surface replacing what's behind it.
  • The Curve Editor's key sidebar scrolls when a short editor crops it.
  • Deep EXRs are recognized from their header, faster.
